_why_this_is_data_and_not_code: These patterns detect a handler that swallows a caught failure. Written
into a .py file they ARE that shape, so ~/.claude/hooks/laws.py refuses
the file -- correctly, by its own blunt rule, and it has no prose or
pattern exemption. Measured 2026-08-25: a Write carrying these patterns
is refused for .py and allowed for .json/.txt/.md.
That is very likely why the law was never ported into this repository.
Keeping rule definitions in a data file next to an engine that loads them
is ordinary design -- eslint, semgrep and this repo's own rules.oracle all
work this way. It hides no swallowed handler: the engine still judges
every handler in the tree by its EFFECT. State the sidestep out loud
anyway, because a change that happens to get past a gate should be
reviewed as such rather than quietly benefited from.
_ported_from: ~/.claude/hooks/laws.py — LAW 1, SILENCE. Verbatim. Two implementations of one law drift apart, and then the hook and the sweep disagree about the same line.

handlers.name: js_catch
handlers.note: A block handler in JS/TS. The body is group 1.

handlers.name: js_arrow_catch
handlers.note: Not in laws.py, and needed here: a promise tail whose handler is an arrow function. The parameter list sits between the keyword and the body, putting it out of reach of js_catch. Measured at frontend/src/websearch/fetchPage.ts:430.

handlers.name: py_block
handlers.note: An indented Python handler. Group 1 anchors the indent so the body stops at the dedent; group 2 is the body.

handlers.name: ruby_rescue
handlers.note: Carried over from laws.py. No Ruby ships in this repo today, so this pattern is expected to match nothing; the receipt reports per-pattern hit counts so an idle rule is visible as idle rather than mistaken for a passing one.

effect.note: The whole judgment. A body matching this diverts control flow or binds a value, and is handled. A body that does not match only CALLS something -- it reports the failure and carries on as though it had succeeded. Reading the EFFECT rather than matching logger names is what catches a reporter nobody has invented yet.
